newsitem.title: USA: Newmont gets SEC ok in bid for Santa Fe.
newsitem.headline: Newmont gets SEC ok in bid for Santa Fe.

text.p: Newmont Mining Corp says the Securities and Exchange Commission will not object to its use of pooling of interests accounting in a merger with Santa Fe Pacific Gold if Santa Fe pays a $65 million fee to end its merger pact with Homestake Mining Co.
Newmont issued the statement late Wednesday, attributing the information to SEC staff.
The break-up charge contained in Santa Fe's merger pact with Homestake Mining had threatened Newmont's proposal to use pooling of interests accounting in a combination with Santa Fe.

The companies have been entwined in a take-over struggle since December, when Newmont made an unsolicited offer for Santa Fe, which entered a friendly merger pact with Homestake Mining four days later.
Newmont has raised its offer to 0.4 Newmont share for each Santa Fe share.
Santa Fe said earlier this month that it was still weighing the offer against the Homestake proposal, which would give 1.115 Homestake shares for each Santa Fe share.
Santa Fe shares were unchanged Wednesday at 17-3/8, and Homestake Mining shares were unchanged at 16.
